findings.title: art:import: a corrupt pack PNG crashes instead of being listed, and duplicate output paths silently overwrite each other
findings.claim: During validation, readPng is called on every existing pack without a try/catch. A truncated or non-PNG file therefore throws out of runImport, so the CLI dies with a stack trace instead of the one-line problem list the spec describes. Separately, two outputs that resolve to the same path both pass validation; the second writeFileSync overwrites the first while both sheets still appear on the contact sheet. 'Nothing written on failure' still holds, because all writes come after validation.
findings.evidence: .superpowers/sdd/art-i-a-branch.diff L262-264 (importCore: `existsSync(packPath)` then `const img = readPng(packPath)` with no catch); L271-274 (each output is written in turn with no check for a repeated resolved path); L259-260 (the only output check is the paid/ prefix); spec L39 ('each produce one line; the script lists every problem and exits 1'). This is also the Task 6 minor in progress.md L278.
findings.why: Art-ii is the first real user of this script. A bad download or a copy-paste slip in art/import.json then gives a crash or a silently missing sheet rather than a clear problem line. It does not block Art-i-a, because the committed list is empty.
findings.fix: In the validation loop, wrap the read: `try { img = readPng(packPath) } catch (e) { problems.push(`outputs[${i}]: pack file ${o.pack} is not a readable PNG (${(e as Error).message})`); return; }`. Keep a `Map<string, number>` of resolved output paths and push `outputs[${i}]: output ${o.output} is also written by outputs[${j}]` when one repeats. Optionally refuse outputs that do not end in `.png`. Add one test for each.

findings.title: artImport tests: the tie-break assertion cannot fail, and the packing test checks only the sheet size
findings.claim: The 'ties go to the earlier palette colour' check uses a palette of two identical colours, `[0x808080, 0x808080]`. Either index returns 0x808080, so a last-wins bug would still pass. The packing test asserts only the 16x16 sheet size, so a frame written to the wrong cell, or a swapped x/y in the cell maths, would also pass.
findings.evidence: artImport.test.ts in the diff L1269-1270 (`createRemap([0x808080, 0x808080])` then `toBe(0x808080)`); L1300-1305 (the packing test checks only `[sheet.width, sheet.height]`). The implementation itself is correct: diff L194 uses a strict `d < bestD`, so the first colour wins a tie, and L231 places frame i at cell `(i % columns) * cw, floor(i / columns) * ch`. Spec L40 (ties broken by palette order) and L43 (tests for the remap).
findings.why: The test that claims to cover a spec rule cannot detect its violation. I put it at P2 rather than P1 because I checked the current code by reading it and it is right.
findings.fix: Split the nearest-colour search out of createRemap into `nearestIndex(labs: Lab[], lab: Lab): number` and test an exact tie with hand-built Lab values, e.g. `nearestIndex([[0,0,0],[2,0,0]], [1,0,0]) === 0`. In the packing test, give each frame a distinct opaque colour and assert the top-left pixel of cells (0,0), (1,0) and (0,1).

findings.title: Floor-art sub-textures are not destroyed on a rebuild, and the door-floor skip has no test
findings.claim: floorSprite makes a new Texture on the shared source for every floor part. The rebuild path calls `c.destroy()` with no options, so those sub-Textures are never destroyed; in Pixi 8 a Texture also registers a listener on its source, so they accumulate on every layout change. Separately, tileLayer.test checks the sprite count only with a loose lower bound, and nothing tests that a door tile's floor fill is skipped when floor art is ready.
findings.evidence: tiles.ts in the diff L1016 (`new Texture({ source: tex.source, frame: ... })` for each part); L1028 (`for (const c of floorArt.removeChildren()) c.destroy();`); L1052 (`if (p.floor && !art)`); tileLayer.test.ts in the diff L1712-1714 (`toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(floorTiles)`). Task 5 minors are in progress.md L277.
findings.why: The leak only grows on a layout change, which is rare, and the art path is off until Art-ii, so nothing is visible today. It will matter once paid floors ship.
findings.fix: Use `c.destroy({ texture: true, textureSource: false })` (or cache one sub-Texture per name and part). In tileLayer.test, assert the exact sprite count for the Cutter, and assert that with art on the `doors` Graphics draws no full-tile floor rectangle on a door tile.

findings.title: The shadowing test's title claims a paid-over-free case that it never builds
findings.claim: The test titled 'refuses a paid file that shadows a free entry by binding its name' builds a free/free clash (font.m5x7) and a paid/paid clash (house.floor.2), but never the paid-over-free case the spec rule is about. The rule itself is generic, so the code is correct.
findings.evidence: paidManifest.test.ts in the diff L1574-1578; manifest.ts in the diff L786-790 (the generic owner map); spec L31. Task 4 minor in progress.md L276.
findings.why: A misleading title on a spec-rule test.
findings.fix: Add a free `raw/` entry that binds `house.floor.0` next to the `paid` entry and expect `/house\.floor\.0 is already bound/`, or rename the test.

Door geometry matches plan Decision 7 (diff L395-433). PANEL_THICK 12 / BAND 10. panelWidth = 2*round(8(1-p)), panels drawn when w > 0. Jambs {0,8,2,16} and {30,8,2,16}. Seam {16,10,2,12}. Bar {10,14,12,4}. Ticks {2,8,2,16} and {28,8,2,16}. Stripes start at even offsets because the panels are even. The panel stroke is PANEL_STROKE 2 with alignment 1, and node_modules/pixi.js FillTypes.d.ts confirms 1 means inside in Pixi 8.19. The seam overlaps the right panel's inside stroke, so the closed seam does not flicker when panels meet at small progress.

Walls: light and shadow are computed per segment as in Decision 8 (diff L1112-1123), and the draw order is band, shadow, light (tiles.ts in the diff L1040-1042). Every edge lies inside the tile on its own band (the wallModel test sweeps 4^5 neighbourhoods, diff L1772-1778), so no edge is drawn over a neighbour's band or a door. consoleModel.WALL_GAP follows automatically (11 to 10, consoleModel.ts:L17). The desk sits flush below the band and does not cover the shadow edge.

On door tiles the door picture's floor fill covers them when art is off (tiles.ts:L64), as Decision 9 says. With art on, door tiles get a whole-tile sprite in build and the door floor fill is skipped (tiles.ts:L64).

Paid manifest: the file regex now accepts paid/ (diff L753). The superRefine rules are paid if and only if the file is under paid/, required false, an http(s) source, a retrieved date and a credit line (diff L772-778). The duplicate-name rule skips entries that already failed the name-or-sheet rule (diff L786). For free entries the notices still go through the unchanged non-paid branches (creditsText.ts:L16, L22), so free output is byte-identical; Task 4 recorded `npm run credits` with no diff. buildCreditLines needs no change (creditsText.ts:L38). LICENSE_URLS excludes paid and original (licenses.ts:L9). .gitignore adds public/assets/paid/ and .art/ (diff L15-17). house.floor.0-3 are optional and grouped as the houseFloor feature (diff L337, L708).

Import script: validation runs before any write and returns early on any problem (diff L269). Alpha below 128 becomes 0,0,0,0, otherwise the pixel is opaque and set to the nearest palette colour in OKLab with first-wins ties (diff L194, L200-205). Output is fixed 8-bit RGBA from pngjs (diff L214-217). The contact sheet is at 2x on ROLE.background with a 4 px gap. The CLI sets exitCode 1 on problems and 0 on the empty list (diff L132-137). A missing source folder is a problem even with an empty list (Decision 14, accepted).
